chapter: Beginnings and early New Orleans scene
title: Born 1906 and taking up the drums
summary: Williams was born in New Orleans in 1906 and loved drums, following parades and bass drummers like Black Benny. His mother bought him a snare drum, and he went on to play with Joseph Thomas before forming a group with Lawrence Marrero and George Lewis.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Yeah, you want to start now. Born here in New Orleans, 1906 September 22nd. Raised in New Orleans. Raised in New Orleans. What's that? Right here. Down Philly Shandris Street. Which? Philly Shandris. Down the night war. That's what I was born at. Did you hear much music around the house, your family play around the house? Oh wow, I follow the, I like it. I follow the music and drums. Drums were really my, drum was really my, my praise. Sticking. Sticking. Sticking. Sticking. Sticking.
You were talking about how drums were your craved, huh?

Yeah, yeah, I loved it. I loved the drums. I used to go to the Lyrics Theater and they had this guy, you're a red happy drummer. And this was my seat in the show, right by him. He had more runs than anybody in the world. And this guy, his brother, I played with him, Lil Jim, he died, bass drummer, Black Benny. I used to follow the parades. He was playing with Papa Celestan. And I used to carry his bass drum. And when they had a job, a parade when I'd leave, and from Chris Kelly, he had Faso and Mila Barnes was playing with Faso as a drummer. And I used to bang on his drums. So finally my mother bought me a snare drum. Oh I had the touch and all, you know what I mean? So she bought me a snare drum and I waged around and got me a bass drum. And then I used to play for them. They had a lot of piano and drums in. Parties? Yeah, dances. Yeah, real, change things. That's what they really was using, piano and drums in the houses, you know what I mean? This was house parties, not a big dance. No, house parties. Piano and drums was using at that time. They would, you know. So then after finally, when I was making my career, I was going along with Joseph Thomas. Worked with him about for five years. And then after Joseph Thomas, well I commenced getting a lot of work myself, you see. Going around we had a good hustle for the band, you know what I mean? So therefore we had to split up. But that's me and Lawrence, Marrero, and George Lewis took in together, you see. Because I was in between time working in the WPA band. See, Said Frazier was my teacher. See I used to set set beside Said Frazier and George Riley and Ernest Chapania. After Ernest Chapania used to send me out on a lot of these jobs because he was a real street man. Ernest Chapania was, I know you're a talker. He was a real street man on the street. He was Celestine Head Man and the Brass Man. Because Chani Babi was his orchestra drummer. But he didn't like to play in the orchestra much? Who that? Trapania. No, no, no. He didn't care. Every time he had something he'd call on me and send me. No, he didn't care too much. I guess probably after he was getting old, you know, older and older, you see. Probably the time when I was doing the WPA time, you know.
How old do you figure he was? Much older than you, huh?
Who, Ernest Chapania? Oh yeah, Ernest Chapania was an old man.
No, I couldn't excimate on that. I couldn't excimate on that. I knew he was an older man than me. I was a youngster.
